heroNote: MIT code · CC BY-NC-SA fiction · no accounts, no tracking.
premiseBody: CIRCA — the Commission for Incident Review and Corrective Action — is not a government agency. It is a continuity: a bureaucracy that has attached itself to whatever power structure was available for long enough that nobody remembers its first name. It reviews incidents that should not have happened, and files reports about them. It does not correct reality. It files paperwork on it.
premiseBodyTwo: The archive is a story and an interface at the same time. Every record is authored as Markdown, and every record is also a plate of codes, clearance levels, redactions, and citations that point at other records. The worldbuilding lives in that machinery: a document that behaves like paperwork is easier to believe than one that behaves like prose.
quote: CIRCA does not decide what is true. It decides what is on file.
quoteAttribution: Central principle of the Commission — in fiction, and in the code.
specimenText: A free-standing door in a pasture in Gangwon Province. No walls. No frame beyond the door itself. It has been there for at least sixty years, possibly longer. It does not move. It does not open on its own. It is, by every available measure, a door.
specimenNote: One of the authored records. Sample content, not canon.
editionsTitle: The same records, read two ways.
editionsLede: Everything on this site is one of two things: something you read, or something you operate. Both editions render the same corpus from the same source.
readingBody: A typographic reading edition, prerendered on the server. Every record has its own page, its own citation trail, and its own copy of the Markdown it was built from. It is complete without JavaScript, and it is the version worth quoting.
workstationBody: A workstation that behaves like the operating system of an institution that never existed: a record viewer, a correspondence client, a filing desk. It runs on illustrative fixtures, and it saves nothing.
editionsNote: Both editions are previews. There is no backend, and notes and drafts stay in the browser.
builtLede: The fiction is the easy part. Most of the work is the machinery that keeps one record legible in both editions.
factRecordsDetail: Markdown with frontmatter, authored by hand. No CMS, no database, no editor.
factPipelineDetail: remark, with plugins that withhold redacted text, resolve figure directives, and anchor headings. One parsed document feeds both editions.
factPagesDetail: Next.js App Router. Every record page is prerendered for both languages; the index, directory, and search render on demand.
factInterfaceDetail: React server components and CSS Modules. No component library on the reading edition, and no client JavaScript there.
factLanguageDetail: English and Korean, routed at /en and /ko. One catalog per language; no sentence is written inside a component.
factTestsDetail: Vitest for the interface and its rules. The pre-commit hook runs lint, typecheck, and the suite before anything lands.
factLicenceDetail: MIT for the code, Creative Commons for the fiction. Both are set out further down this page.
builtNote: The backend is planned and not built. There are no accounts, no database, and no telemetry on this site.
contributeTitle: The archive grows by being written.
contributeLede: CIRCA Archive is pre-production and open. Records, continuities, organizations, interface work, and corrections are all welcome — and no contributor is asked to sign anything.
stepGuideBody: Scope, conventions, and an honest account of what is finished. A proposed continuity belongs in an issue before it becomes a pull request.
stepChangeBody: One coherent change per branch, with the lockfile committed and generated folders left alone.
stepChecksBody: The pre-commit hook verifies staged READMEs, repository tooling, lint, types, and the unit suite.
contributeNote: Correspondence about the fiction, the code, or a broken record belongs in the repository's issues.
contributorsLede: CIRCA Archive is maintained in the open. Anyone who writes a record, corrects a page, or files a useful report is credited here — there is no agreement to sign and no account to create.
contributorsMaintainerWork: Records, interface, and the archive's estate.
contributorsNote: Records carry their author's name beside the seal. Everything else is credited here and in the commit history.
supportBody: CIRCA Archive is a personal design and worldbuilding project. No company sits behind it, and nothing here is for sale. Support pays for the domain, the hosting, and the hours it takes to read pull requests and keep the archive's records consistent with one another.
supportSponsorBody: Recurring or one-time, through GitHub Sponsors. No tier, no badge, no obligation.
supportPromise: Nothing on this site is paywalled. The records, the source, and the licence stay open either way.
faqLede: The questions that arrive most often, with the answers the project actually gives.
faqRealA: No. The Commission, its offices, its correspondents, and every incident on file are invented. The site names no real agency and describes no real event. The interface, the records, and the argument for them are real work.
faqWriteA: That is the point of the archive. Read the contribution guide, open an issue with the continuity you have in mind, then file the record as Markdown. Records are reviewed for consistency with what is already on file, not for canon.
faqNotesA: Nowhere yet. There is no backend: notes, drafts, and replies live in the browser tab and are lost when it closes. Nothing you type is transmitted or stored.
faqReuseQ: Can I reuse the records or the code?
faqReuseA: The code is MIT. The records, the fiction, and the artwork are CC BY-NC-SA 4.0: share and adapt them with attribution, non-commercially, under the same licence. The seal belongs to the fiction.
faqLanguageA: English is the language the archive's paperwork was written in; Korean is there because the Commission keeps correspondents in the Republic of Korea. Neither is a translation of the other: every page, record, and label exists in both.
faqRoadmapQ: What is finished, and what is not?
faqRoadmapA: The reading edition and the workstation preview are done. The backend is drafted and not built; accounts, saved annotations, and persistence are future work. Until then this is a reading edition, and it says so.
contactLede: Three doors. None of them needs an account, and all of them reach the same maintainer.
channelBugBody: A page that will not render, a record that will not open, a link that dead-ends, a table that will not align.
channelFeatureBody: A missing affordance, a new continuity, a better way to read the citation web.
channelContactBody: Press, permissions, a record that carries your name, or anything the two forms above do not cover.
contactNote: Reports and proposals are read in the open, in the repository. Nothing sent from this page is stored by the site itself.
licenceTitle: MIT for the code. CC for the fiction.
licenceLede: The repository holds two different kinds of thing, so it carries two licences. The terms are short, because there is almost nothing here to accept.
licenceCodeBody: The application, the render pipeline, and the stylesheets. Use it, change it, ship it — keep the copyright notice.
licenceContentBody: The records, the fiction, and the artwork. Share and adapt them with attribution, non-commercially, under the same licence.
licenceFiction: Nothing here is real. No agency, office, correspondent, or incident described on this site exists.
licenceAccounts: There are no accounts and no payments, and the site collects no correspondence.
licenceCookie: One cookie remembers your language. No analytics, no third-party scripts, no profile.
licenceWarranty: Provided as is. Nothing on this site is advice, an offer, or a service.
licenceFootnote: Corrections, takedowns, and reports go to the repository's issues.
footerTagline: A bureaucracy for incidents that should not have happened, written in public and filed in Markdown.
footerFiction: This is a work of fiction. No agency, office, correspondent, or incident described on this site is real.
homeLede: CIRCA Archive is a fictional institution and a working interface: a bureaucracy that files invented incidents in real Markdown, then reads them back in two editions. The records are fictional. The machinery is open source.
homePremiseTitle: A bureaucracy for things that should not have happened.
docsTeaserLede: Nine pages on the renderer, the record format, the routes, the tests, and the three design systems — written for the code as it stands, not as it is planned.
aboutPageLede: CIRCA Archive is a fictional continuity and an open-source interface. This page is the long account: the premise, both editions, how the records are built, how to join in, who is on file, how the work is supported, and the terms.
docsOverviewLede: How the archive is built, how a record is written, and how to change either without breaking the other. Nine pages, in the order a contributor needs them.
docsOverviewWhatBody: CIRCA Archive is two things at once. In fiction it is the public face of the Commission for Incident Review and Corrective Action: a continuity that files reports on incidents that should not have happened. In code it is a Next.js application that renders that invented archive in English and Korean, with a server-rendered reading edition and an interactive workstation preview.
docsOverviewWhatBodyTwo: The records are invented. The interface, the renderer, the tests, and this documentation are real work. The site has no backend and no persistence, and nothing you type is stored.
docsOverviewWhatCalloutBody: It describes the repository, not the fiction. The archive's own reading guide is at the public archive, under About the archive.
docsStartCard1Body: Install both toolchains, run the site, and know which command proves a change.
docsStartCard2Body: The header fields, the section rules, redactions, figures, and where the corpus lives.
docsStartCard3Body: One coherent change, the checks that prove it, and a pull request that says what you verified.
docsOverviewEditionsBody: One corpus, three surfaces. A change to a record or an index entry appears wherever that record is read.
docsOverviewEditionsReadingBody: server-rendered pages under /site, readable without JavaScript, with one client island for notes.
docsOverviewEditionsWorkstationBody: a client-side shell under /desktop with draggable windows, five applications, and illustrative fixtures.
docsOverviewEditionsProjectBody: the landing page, this documentation, and the dossier under /meta, written outside the fiction.
docsOverviewEditionsBodyTwo: Both editions read the same index entries and the same Markdown sources. Neither owns content.
docsOverviewStatusBody: The reading edition and the workstation preview work end to end over fixtures. The boundary between what exists and what is planned is part of the interface's honesty.
docsOverviewStatusBuilt: the public portal, the reading edition and record downloads, the workstation and its five applications, the Markdown pipeline, the project pages, and this documentation.
docsOverviewStatusNotBuilt: an API, a database, authentication, saved annotations, moderation, and real full-text search.
docsOverviewStatusPlanned: the .NET 10, EF Core, and SignalR platform described in ARCHITECTURE.md.
docsOverviewStatusCalloutBody: It describes a platform whose API and schema do not exist. The running code is the source of truth for what the interface does today, and these pages document the running code.
docsOverviewReadingBody: The interface is translated into English and Korean; code identifiers, routes, commands, and archive codes are not. This documentation follows the default branch, with no version switcher: the project is pre-production and the tree moves.
docsOverviewReadingBodyTwo: Every page ends with the previous and next topic, and every section has an anchor. The sidebar filters as you type; the right rail lists the sections on the page you are reading.
docsOverviewReadingBodyThree: If a page disagrees with the tree, the tree is right and the page is a bug.
docsGettingStartedLede: From a clean clone to a local build of the archive, in the order the checks run.
docsGettingStartedRequirementsBody: Bun runs the root tooling and the frontend. Next.js supplies the rest; the browser tests are optional.
docsGettingStartedRequirementsOne: Bun 1.3.14 — packages, scripts, and the lockfiles.
docsGettingStartedRequirementsTwo: Node.js 20.9 or newer — required by Next.js.
docsGettingStartedRequirementsThree: Chromium — only for the Playwright suite.
docsGettingStartedRequirementsFour: Git, and a clone of the repository.
docsGettingStartedRequirementsCalloutBod: The repository root and client/ each have their own package.json and lockfile. Install both; the pre-commit hook runs both.
docsGettingStartedInstallBody: Fork and clone, then install at the root and in the client. Both lockfiles are committed, so use the frozen lockfile.
docsGettingStartedInstallBodyTwo: bun run prepare installs the Husky hooks. A commit then checks staged READMEs, repository tooling, lint, types, and the unit suite before it lands.
docsGettingStartedRunBody: Start the development server from client/. It serves port 3001; the proxy redirects bare paths to the reader's language.
docsGettingStartedRunPortal: Public portal, in the Commission's voice
docsGettingStartedRunBodyTwo: A production build is bun run --cwd=client build, then bun run --cwd=client start.
docsGettingStartedVerifyBody: Run the checks you touched. Before a pull request, precommit is the full pass.
docsGettingStartedVerifyCalloutBody: The pull request template asks for verification. Name the commands that passed and the ones that could not run; do not report a suite you did not execute.
docsGettingStartedTroubleBody: Three failures account for most local setup problems.
docsGettingStartedTroubleOne: A read-only Bun cache in a sandbox: set BUN_TMPDIR to a writable directory and pass --cache-dir on install.
docsGettingStartedTroubleTwo: Port 3001 already occupied: stop the other server. Playwright reuses an existing server when one is configured.
docsGettingStartedTroubleThree: Missing Chromium: run bunx playwright install chromium, and set PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH when its cache is not writable.
docsGettingStartedTroubleBodyTwo: If a page prints a message key instead of a sentence, the catalog is missing that key in that language. i18n-messages.test.ts is the test that catches it.
docsStructureLede: Where the routes, the components, the copy, and the corpus actually live.
docsStructureTreeBody: The repository is a small monorepo with one built surface and two reserved ones. Read the top level before the client: most confusion about this project comes from searching the wrong tree.
docsStructureTreeBodyTwo: Reserved folders may be absent from a fresh clone; Git tracks files, not directories.
docsStructureClientBody: The client has three surfaces, each with its own component folder, stylesheet, and README.
docsStructureClientOne: components/archive-site/ — the reading edition: server-rendered pages, search, records, and downloads.
docsStructureClientTwo: components/ — the workstation shell and its five application windows.
docsStructureClientThree: components/meta/ — the project landing page, the dossier, and this documentation.
docsStructureClientFour: components/ui/ — shadcn-style primitives shared by the client surfaces.
docsStructureClientFive: lib/markdown/ — the record renderer. No React, no DOM.
docsStructureClientBodyTwo: A route under app/[lang] composes: it resolves the language, sets the request locale, builds metadata, and renders a component. Copy and layout do not live in the route file.
docsStructureContentBody: What is translated and what is not is a product decision, not an accident.
docsStructureContentBodyTwo: An archive does not translate a document that was filed in English. The catalog test keeps the two languages aligned, and the archive's own guide explains the gap to a reader.
docsStructureReadmeBody: Every authored folder has a README stating what it owns, how it is organised, its boundaries, and how it is verified. bun run check fails when a folder is added without one.
docsStructureReadmeBodyTwo: Stage the README with the code. The pre-commit hook checks staged paths, so an unstaged README does not count.
docsRecordsLede: A record is Markdown with an optional YAML header, and one parse feeds both editions.
docsRecordsAnatomyBody: A record is a single Markdown document. Its YAML header carries the fields; its body is what a reader sees. A level-two heading starts a navigable section; a level-three heading stays inside one.
docsRecordsAnatomyCalloutTitle: The header is data, not body copy
docsRecordsAnatomyCalloutBody: The parser removes the YAML block before rendering. It never prints as text, and it is never sent to the client as a block of prose.
docsRecordsFrontmatterBody: The frontmatter is parsed and kept as metadata. The archive index remains the source of truth for the catalogue, so a record's body can disagree with its own header — one intentionally does. The pipeline reports the disagreement rather than reconciling it.
docsRecordsFrontmatterCode: the record code this filing is cited by.
docsRecordsFrontmatterIncident: the incident the filing belongs to.
docsRecordsFrontmatterTitleRow: the title printed on the sheet.
docsRecordsFrontmatterStatusRow: the filing state as the document declares it.
docsRecordsFrontmatterSeverity: S, A, or B — the classification's severity.
docsRecordsFrontmatterDates: ISO filing day and last revision day.
docsRecordsFrontmatterClassification: the access level and the clearance it requires.
docsRecordsFrontmatterRelated: cross-references and labels; both are lists.
docsRecordsSectionsBody: Use a level-two heading for a section a reader should be able to jump to, and a level-three heading for structure inside it. The reader's page rail is built from level-two headings, and a heading inside a fenced code block is ignored.
docsRecordsSectionsBodyTwo: Record names are set as filing titles; the prose is set in a typed face. There is no rich layout to maintain, which is why a record survives a change of edition.
docsRecordsSectionsCalloutTitle: A sealed section is still on the page
docsRecordsSectionsCalloutBody: The reader frame withholds it; the Markdown still contains it. Content removal is a product decision, not an editing one.
docsRecordsSyntaxBody: The corpus extends GFM with four conventions. Each one is handled by the shared pipeline, so every renderer agrees about it.
docsRecordsSyntaxRedaction: a redaction, held behind paper until the reader opens it.
docsRecordsSyntaxFigure: a figure with an alignment (left, right, full) and a caption.
docsRecordsSyntaxQuote: a blockquote; the filings use it for correspondence and notices.
docsRecordsSyntaxTable: a GFM table. Redactions work inside cells because rows are repaired before parsing.
docsRecordsSyntaxBodyTwo: Raw HTML is not passed through: a script element in a record is text, and enabling raw HTML would make the archive's own syntax legend live markup.
docsRecordsSyntaxBodyThree: Citations to other records are written as /site/records/CODE; the reading edition prefixes the reader's language, because a Markdown document cannot know which edition is reading it.
docsRecordsWhereBody: Bodies live in components/reader/record-sources.ts; index entries live in components/browser/archive-index.ts. A record can be reachable without a body — the reader shows the withheld shape, which is a real state of the interface.
docsRecordsWhereBodyTwo: CIRCA-S-03007 is the renderer's test corpus and is filed in the index on purpose. It exercises the header, a table with redactions, all three figure alignments, quotes, and a code fence.
docsRecordsWhereCalloutBody: Adding a record today means editing those two TypeScript modules. When the backend exists, the renderer should keep taking Markdown and not learn where it came from.
docsRenderingLede: A record is parsed once. The sheet, the text export, and the Markdown download all read the same result.
docsRenderingPipelineBody: parseRecord() in lib/markdown/pipeline.ts returns three things: an mdast tree, the YAML metadata, and a warning list. It does not return HTML, a React element, or a string.
docsRenderingPipelineBodyTwo: The on-screen sheet and the exports share that tree. Two parsers would drift, and the fiction is that a record is one artifact.
docsRenderingPipelineBodyThree: There are two React renderers, not two pipelines: record-prose.tsx renders the tree on the server for the reading edition, and record-markdown.tsx hands the same plugin list to react-markdown in the workstation viewer.
docsRenderingPluginFrontmatter: parses the YAML header and removes the node, so it never reaches the renderers.
docsRenderingPluginGfm: tables, strikethrough, autolinks, and task lists.
docsRenderingPluginNormalise: escapes double pipes inside a table cell before GFM can split the row.
docsRenderingPluginRedaction: turns paired double pipes into redaction nodes in text and inline code.
docsRenderingPluginImage: turns an alignment directive into a figure node, and strips the alignment from the caption.
docsRenderingPluginHeadings: gives each heading a per-parse, collision-free anchor.
docsRenderingPluginsBody: Add a plugin to the shared list, then make every renderer and emitter handle the node it produces. A transform that exists only in the viewer is not part of the pipeline.
docsRenderingWarningsBody: The pipeline collects defects instead of throwing. Only corrupt YAML stops a parse; everything else still renders.
docsRenderingWarningsOne: unmatched-redaction — an odd number of delimiters; the unpaired one stays literal.
docsRenderingWarningsTwo: unknown-image-align — the alignment word is not left, right, or full.
docsRenderingWarningsThree: relative-image — the image cannot be resolved without an asset base.
docsRenderingWarningsFour: metadata-disagreement — the header and the body print different statuses. It is left visible on purpose.
docsRenderingWarningsBodyTwo: A warning is a content defect, not an engineering failure. The test corpus deliberately disagrees with its own header, because the fiction is about records that contradict themselves.
docsRenderingExportsBody: The plain-text export pins redactions to hidden: the withheld words are not in the string at all. The Markdown download serves the authored source, the only copy that contains them.
docsRenderingExportsBodyTwo: Exports are generated from the authored Markdown, not from the rendered page. There is no PDF generation; a record's .pdf name belongs to the fiction.
docsRenderingExportsCalloutTitle: A held filing has no download
docsRenderingExportsCalloutBody: The download route returns 404 for a filing the archive has not released.
docsRenderingBoundariesTitle: What the renderer will not do
docsRenderingBoundariesBody: It never reads the archive index or the record service. It is handed a string and returns data. Keep it that way: the same parse must serve a test, an export, a server page, and a browser without a second implementation.
docsRenderingBoundariesBodyTwo: No raw HTML, no HTML injection, no editor-specific syntax, and no network. Relative figure paths resolve only against an asset base the caller supplies.
docsRoutesLede: Every document answers at one address, in one language, on one of three surfaces.
docsRoutesMapBody: The routes below are the whole public surface. Every one of them is under a language segment.
docsRoutesMapPortal: the public portal, in the Commission's voice.
docsRoutesMapRecords: the record index; the q parameter is filtered on the server.
docsRoutesMapRecord: one record, prerendered for every code in the index.
docsRoutesMapDownload: Markdown and plain-text copies; 404 when the filing is held.
docsRoutesMapRandom: a redirect to a randomly chosen record.
docsRoutesLanguageBody: routing.ts is the only file that lists the languages. The proxy resolves an explicit prefix first, then the NEXT_LOCALE cookie, then Accept-Language, then English.
docsRoutesLanguageBodyTwo: The language layout validates the segment, sets the document language, loads the fonts, and mounts the message provider with only the namespaces client components read.
docsRoutesLanguageCalloutBody: Add it to routing.ts, add a catalog directory under messages/, and translate every key. The catalog test compares key sets, placeholders, and rich-text tags across locales.
docsRoutesEditionsBody: The reading edition is server-first: search is a GET form, downloads are route handlers, and the only client island on a record is the notes composer.
docsRoutesEditionsBodyTwo: The workstation is a client shell: stateful windows over the same fixtures, with no backend. Neither edition owns content, so a change in one corpus appears in both.
docsRoutesAddingBody: A route under the language segment has four jobs: resolve the language, set the request locale, build metadata from the metadata namespace, and render a component.
docsRoutesAddingBodyTwo: Layouts belong to the surface, copy belongs to the catalog, and metadata belongs to the page. Link with the locale-aware Link from the i18n navigation module, never next/link.
docsContributingLede: One coherent change, the checks that prove it, and a pull request that says what you verified.
docsContributingBeforeBody: Read README.md, AGENTS.md, and the documents the change touches. Search issues and pull requests first. Open a proposal for architecture, dependencies, or story mechanics; small corrections can go straight to a pull request.
docsContributingBeforeCalloutBody: ARCHITECTURE.md describes an unbuilt platform; the design and product documents describe intent. If the code and the specification disagree, say so in the issue instead of quietly choosing one.
docsContributingBranchBody: Fork, branch, and keep one change per branch. docs/record-lifecycle and feat/record-editor are the example shapes. Do not mix a refactor with a behaviour change.
docsContributingBranchOne: Commit the lockfiles; do not add a competing package manager lockfile.
docsContributingBranchTwo: Do not commit local environment files, credentials, generated output, or editor settings.
docsContributingBranchThree: Preserve author credit, stable IDs, and display codes.
docsContributingBranchBodyTwo: Write tests first where the change is behavioural: red, green, refactor. No coverage threshold is mandated, and a test that asserts a key rather than a sentence is worse than no test.
docsContributingChecksBody: Before you open a pull request, run what you changed. The full pass is the hook.
docsContributingChecksBodyTwo: The hook verifies staged READMEs, then runs the root tooling tests and the frontend lint, typecheck, and unit suite. A failure is the check working; fix it rather than bypassing it.
docsContributingDocsTitle: Documentation is part of the change
docsContributingDocsBody: Documentation changes with the code. Every authored folder needs a README, every user-facing string needs a key in each language, and a new behaviour needs a test in the project's idiom.
docsContributingDocsOne: New copy: add the key to English, translate Korean, then run the catalog test.
docsContributingDocsTwo: New folder: add README.md and stage it.
docsContributingDocsThree: New interface: screenshots in the pull request, at desktop and mobile widths.
docsContributingDocsFour: Changed route: update metadata and every link the tests hold.
docsContributingPullBody: Use an imperative commit message: Add record creation endpoint. In the pull request, state the problem, the resulting behaviour, the related issue or specification, and exactly what you verified.
docsContributingPullBodyTwo: No contributor licence agreement is required. Submit only work you can licence under MIT, and identify third-party material.
docsContributingPullCalloutBody: Bugs and proposals go to the issue templates. Security reports go through SECURITY.md, never a public issue.
docsTestingLede: The suite holds the interface to what it claims: behaviour, catalogs, corpus parsing, and the two editions.
docsTestingRhythmBody: Write a failing behavioural test first, then the smallest implementation that passes, then refactor with the suite green. This is the repository's rule, not a preference; a test added after the fact tends to assert what the code does rather than what it should.
docsTestingRhythmBodyTwo: Prioritise authorization, lifecycle transitions, vote uniqueness, and visibility when those exist. Today, prioritise the renderer, the archive rules, and the catalog contract.
docsTestingUnitBody: Vitest runs in jsdom. Tests live in client/tests/ and are named for the surface or module they hold.
docsTestingUnitPipeline: parse, redactions, figures, warnings, and the corpus contract.
docsTestingUnitArchive: the reading edition, record pages, downloads, and the project pages.
docsTestingUnitCatalog: catalog key parity, placeholders, rich tags, and empty values.
docsTestingUnitDesktop: the workstation shell, its windows, and their interactions.
docsTestingUnitWindows: geometry, stacking, minimize, maximize, and drag state.
docsTestingUnitBodyTwo: Components that read copy need the provider. Use renderWithIntl from tests/intl.tsx, which loads the real catalogs, so a test asserts the sentence a reader sees rather than a message key.
docsTestingCatalogBody: The catalog test compares the English and Korean catalogs key by key. It also checks placeholders, rich-text tags, empty values, balanced markup, and that a few prose strings are actually translated.
docsTestingCatalogBodyTwo: Add the English key first, then the Korean. A component that reads a missing key renders the key path, which is why this test is the one that catches a half-finished translation.
docsTestingE2eBody: Playwright runs against a real server on port 3001, configured in playwright.config.ts with Chromium. The suite covers responsive behaviour and language routing.
docsTestingE2eBodyTwo: The config starts bun run dev unless a server is already running. In a sandbox, set PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH to a writable directory.
docsTestingCoverageBody: There is no coverage threshold. A useful test names the failure it prevents. A test that renders a component and asserts it exists prevents a crash, not a regression; a test that asserts the wrong document is refused prevents a leak.
docsTestingCoverageBodyTwo: Known gaps are recorded in the per-surface READMEs. The archive's internal search still matches English class and status words, and the reader's relative timestamps remain English. Do not silently narrow a gap in a test.
docsDesignLede: The repository speaks in three registers. Which one you are in decides almost every visual choice.
docsDesignSystemsBody: CIRCA Archive is not one design system. It is three, each answering a different question.
docsDesignSystemsWorkstationRule: 1990s institutional software: steel, bevels, dense chrome, 12px. Never use it outside the desktop.
docsDesignSystemsReadingRule: paper, ink, a serif masthead, filed documents. Depth is a bevel; no gradients.
docsDesignSystemsProjectRule: near-black, bone, ember, serif display, mono labels, a hairline field. Not bound by the workstation rules.
docsDesignSystemsCalloutTitle: The project page is the exception
docsDesignSystemsCalloutBody: It is allowed to look unlike the archive because it answers a different question. The archive links here only through a labelled button.
docsDesignTokensBody: The project page's tokens are declared once on .meta-page in components/meta/meta.css. Use them, and do not introduce a fourth accent.
docsDesignTokensInk: the near-black canvas behind every page.
docsDesignTokensBone: primary text, the solid key, and the specimen sheet.
docsDesignTokensMist: secondary text and labels; the smaller size is for captions.
docsDesignTokensEmber: index numerals, links, focus rings, and the one accent. Never the only signal.
docsDesignTokensLine: rules and borders at 14% bone; the soft variant divides sections.
docsDesignTokensSerif: the argument: display headlines, section titles, quotations, and names.
docsDesignTokensSans: reading copy and controls; 16–17px for body text.
docsDesignTokensMono: every label, index, caption, command, and code sample.
docsDesignTokensBodyTwo: The meta scope also carries the shadcn variables, so a primitive from components/ui inherits this palette without restyling globals. Keep meta styles scoped: the workstation stylesheet must not reach in, and this one must not reach out.
docsDesignPatternsBody: The field is the visual signature: a measured grid with edge hatching, corner crosses, mono status rails, and a halftone plate built from CSS dot screens. It is decoration, always aria-hidden.
docsDesignPatternsOne: One focal point per screen, then a second, then the rest.
docsDesignPatternsTwo: Hairlines instead of cards. A card is a surface, not a default wrapper.
docsDesignPatternsThree: Numbers and labels in mono; the argument in serif; reading copy in sans.
docsDesignPatternsFour: One accent. If everything is ember, nothing is.
docsDesignPatternsBodyTwo: The reference for the landing page is an instrument panel, not a brochure: status lines, plates, measured margins. Add detail a person can read, not noise.
docsDesignAccessBody: Target WCAG 2.2 AA. Project-page text uses bone or mist on near-black; ember is for labels, numerals, and focus, and never the only carrier of meaning.
docsDesignAccessOne: Every interactive element has a visible focus ring: 2px ember, offset.
docsDesignAccessTwo: Motion is one short arrival; honour prefers-reduced-motion.
docsDesignAccessThree: Every plate, chart, and screenshot is decoration with a text caption or aria-hidden.
docsDesignAccessFour: Navigation and language switching are keyboard reachable; the mobile drawer traps focus through Radix Dialog.
docsDesignAccessFive: Content reflows at 320px and 200% zoom without losing function.
docsDesignAccessBodyTwo: Check contrast and focus when you change a control. They are part of the design, not a cleanup pass.
docsDesignAddingBody: A project page is a server component under the meta route, wrapped by the shared chrome. Copy goes in the locale's meta catalog; styles go in meta.css under .meta-page. A documentation page adds a topic in docs-topics.ts and its sections in docs-content.tsx.
docsDesignAddingBodyTwo: Do not add a page that reaches into the archive's chrome or the workstation's bevels. Do not add a second font, a gradient, or a shadow to make something feel finished. The system's job is restraint with one strong gesture.
